observations: Each of the 12 assets is an ordered list of 10 coordinate pairs in a 0-100 space. Assets a01-a03 form closed ring-like outlines of increasing size; a04-a06 are staircase-like step sequences; a07-a09 are zigzag wave sequences; a10-a12 are smooth monotone arcs. Each asset has exactly 10 points. INPUT.json lists 8 directed connections in three chains (a01->a02->a03, a04->a05->a06, a07->a08->a09, a10->a11->a12), each connecting assets of the same apparent family.
interpretation: I focused on the shape families visible in the coordinate lists and converted each asset into a radial signature: each point's distance from the asset centroid becomes a radius at an angle proportional to its index. This turns ordered point lists into closed glyph-like forms whose silhouettes make within-family differences (e.g. a07 vs a09 zigzag amplitude, or ring size growth a01->a03) easy to compare at a glance.
new_relation_or_transformation: Transformation: centroid-distance polar re-encoding of each asset's 10-point sequence into a smooth closed glyph (Catmull-Rom interpolation), laid out in a 4x3 grid preserving the INPUT.json asset order. The supplied connections are drawn only as faint dashed links between glyph centers, as a record of juxtaposition, not as evidence of influence.
possible_dependence_on_input: The glyph radii and shapes depend entirely on the supplied coordinates; the grid order follows INPUT.json's asset_ids list; the dashed links reuse the supplied connection records. Different input data would yield different glyphs.
limitations: The radial re-encoding discards absolute position and orientation of each asset's point list; point index drives angle, so the original ordering choice affects each glyph's silhouette. The visual similarity grouping is an observation about coordinates only; the trace does not establish causation, provenance, or emergence. Connections were treated as opaque directed records.
